# Lumen Cards: overview for AI agents

Lumen Cards is a library of glass-style custom cards for Home Assistant Lovelace dashboards. One JavaScript bundle registers every card. Each card is set up in Home Assistant's visual editor or in YAML, and the interface is available in English and Polish, following the user's Home Assistant profile.

- Repository: https://github.com/dkej123/lumen-cards (MIT)
- Live demo of every card, on a made-up home: https://dkej123.github.io/lumen-cards/
- Requires Home Assistant 2026.6 or newer.
- Install with HACS: add the repository as a custom repository of type **Dashboard**, then download Lumen Cards. Without HACS: copy `dist/lumen-cards.js` and `dist/*.woff2` to `config/www/lumen-cards/` and add `/local/lumen-cards/lumen-cards.js` as a JavaScript module.

## What you can build

- A full dashboard in a `sections` view, with cards for lights, people, alarm, locks, doors, sensors, air quality, climate, weather, covers, media, fans, numbers, selects, calendars and purifiers.
- One-tap scenes and scripts as chips or buttons, including buttons that wait for a device's response.
- Floating buttons on phones, stacking by themselves, with a panel that can hold any cards.
- Pop-ups opened by a URL hash, a navigation bar, section titles and a greeting.
- Stacks with one maximum width for a whole group, and a glass bar of compact tiles.
- An animated weather background for a view, with optional effects on the cards.
- Lights behind relays: one bulb on a relay, or a group of bulbs behind several switches.
- Different layouts for phone and computer, using Home Assistant's `screen` visibility condition. The boundary is a 1024 px viewport.

## How to work with it

- Card config: `type: custom:lumen-<name>-card`, plus the fields of that card. Unknown keys are ignored silently, so take option names from the card's file below. Do not guess them.
- A bad config does not fail on save: the card renders an error card with the reason. Check the rendered dashboard, not only the save result.
- Read the live state list and use only entity ids you have seen there. Ids in these documents are examples.
- Alarm, lock and gate entities are real devices. Do not call their services or run their scripts to test a card. The same goes for any `script` or `button` whose effect you do not know.
- Do not put tokens, addresses or real names into the repository.
